full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque, J: In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order No. 61 dated 7-8-2018 passed by the Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka (respondent No. 3) in Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2009 as evidenced by (Annexure-'F') to the writ petition allowing the application under Order 6, rule 17 and Order 1, rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure should not be declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Shorn of unnecessary details, fact of the case lies in a very short compus. Respondent Nos. 5-12, as petitioner, filed an application under Order 21, rules 58 and 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with sections 32(2) and 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM 2003, in Execution Case No. 105 of 2002 claiming title in the case property. The bank contested the case by filing written objection and additional written objection. The execution court heard the Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2009 and after hearing by its judgment and order dated 5-11-2009 dismissed the same. 

 3. Being aggrieved, the petitioners moved before the District Judge by filing Miscellaneous Appeal No. 312 of 2009 which was dismissed on 3-3-2009. Thereafter, the petitioner in Miscellaneous Case filed Civil Revision No. 1848 of 2010 before this Court in which the rule was made absolute. Against the judgment and order of this Court the bank preferred CPLA No. 1469 of 2011 and the auction purchaser preferred CPLA No. 1498 of 2011. In those appeals the Appellate Division set-aside the judgment and order of this Court and sent back the case to the execution court on remand for fresh trial by its judgment and order dated 24-1-2016. After arrival of record before the execution court the petitioners in miscellaneous case filed an application under Order 6, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for amendment of their application. The bank filed written objection against the application for amendment. The petitioners also filed an application under Order 1, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for adding the auction purchaser opposite party. The execution court heard the applications for amendment of original application and addition of party and after hearing by its judgment and order dated 7-8-2018 allowed both the applications. At this juncture, the auction purchaser moved this Court by filing this writ petition and obtained the present Rule Nisi and order of stay. 

 4. Mr Md Hasanat Parvez, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that proposed amendment has changed the nature and character of the main application as the petitioners introduced new facts contrary to the statements made in the application at the time of filing of the same. He further argued that law does not allow a petitioner or plaintiff to alter the nature and character of the plaint or application by introducing inconsistent and contradictory facts to the detriment of the other party, as such, the execution court has committed illegality in allowing the application for amendment of main application filed under Order 21, rules 58 and 90 CPC and sections 32(2) and 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. In support of his such submissions he has referred to a catena of cases Mollah Shahidul Islam vs Md Monsur Rahman and others reported in 57 DLR 164, Shahajadpur Central Co-operative Bank Ltd. vs Md Majibur Rahman and others reported in 1998 BLD (AD) 81 = 50 DLR (AD) 86, Nazrul Islam Majumder (Md) vs Tahamina Akhtar alias Nahid and another reported in 42 DLR 235, M/s City Ice and Cold Storage Ltd. vs Nitai Chandra Shah and others reported in 1983 BLD (AD) 268, Abdus Salam vs Korban Ali and another reported in 48 DLR 372 and Khaledur Reza Chowdhury vs Saleha Begum and others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 209. 

 6. He further submits that it is the settled principle of law that the plaintiff cannot file an application seeking amendment of plaint which may change the nature and character of the suit introducing inconsistent and contradictory fact, but in the present case the petitioners in miscellaneous case filed the application for amendment of their petition only adding some statement which are absolutely relating to the document filed before the court and it was filed pursuant to the direction and observations made by the Hon'ble Appellate Division in disposing CPLA Nos. 1498 and1469 of 2011, as such, the nature and character of the application in Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2009 has not been changed in any way. Moreover, the opposite party can agitate and deny the facts by filing written objection and by cross examining the witnesses at the time of hearing of the miscellaneous case. 

 7. It is also argued that admittedly that the proposed amendment brings some new facts which are necessary for disposal of the dispute between the parties, as such, the execution court committed no illegality in accepting the amendment of the main application. In support of his submissions he has referred to the cases of Abdul Wadud contractor and another vs Nazir Ahmed and others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 120, M/s Bangladesh Rubber Industries and another vs Begum Lutfunessa and another reported in 1983 BLD (AD) 220, Abdul Rouf (Md) alias Nayan vs State and another reported in 53 DLR 283 and Sunil Chandra Mondal and others vs Narayan Chandra Shil and others reported in 50 DLR (AD) 148. 

 9. The bank filed Execution Case No. 105 of 2002 for execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 27 of 2001 in favour of the bank in which the bank obtained a certificate under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain to sell the property at their instance. Accordingly, the bank published an auction notice on 12-7-2009 for sale of the property fixing 30-7-2009 for submission of quotation and the property was sold in auction on 19-8-2009. The respondent Nos. 5-12 as petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2009 under Order 21, rules 58 and 90 of the Code read with sections 32(2) and 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, which was dismissed by the execution court vide the judgment and order dated 5-1-2009. Thereafter, they preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 312 of 2009 before the District Judge which was also disallowed on 3-3-2010. Thereafter, Civil Revision No. 1148 of 2010 was preferred in which the Rule was made absolute. Against the judgment and order of this Division the bank and the auction purchaser preferred CPLA Nos. 1469 and 1998 of 2011 respectively before the Appellate Division in which the appeals was allowed on 24-1-2016 and sent back the case to the execution court on remand for fresh trial. Thereafter, the petitioners in Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2009 filed an application seeking amendment of their original application proposing some facts to be added and wanting deletion of some statements made in the application. The application was opposed by the bank as well as the present petitioner. The execution court by the impugned judgment and order dated 7-8-2018 allowed the application, hence, the present writ petition. 

 10. It is true that the plaintiff or applicant in any proceeding cannot alter the nature and character of the suit or the application by introducing new, inconsistent and contradictory fact to the detriment of the other party. It is also settled that Order 6, rule 17 of the Code provides that the court may at any stage of the proceedings can allow either party to alter or amend their pleadings in such manner and on such terms as may be just and necessary for the purpose of determining the real questions in controversy between the parties. From perusal of application for amendment, we find that the petitioners in miscellaneous case wanted to add some statements as paragraph '1Ka"8Ka', and '8Kha' and to add a schedule describing the same as disputed land which was sold in auction and wanted to delete some statements in different paragraphs relating to knowledge of the auction and other admitted facts. 

 11. From perusal of judgment and order passed by the Appellate Division in the above mentioned 2 (two) CPLAs, it appears that the court observed that present respondent Nos. 5-12, as petitioner, in Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2019 submitted some documents which were not filed before the execution court and observed that it is imperative on the part of the execution court to consider those documents. In the event of considering the documents so have been filed by the petitioners in miscellaneous case, statements in that regard should be made in the main application. Accordingly, the petitioners in Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2019 by filing an application wanted to introduce such facts relating to documents filed in court. We find that by way of amendment the nature and character of the main application has not been changed in any way rather those statements by way of amendment is necessary for the purpose of determining real questions in controversy. 

 12. In that view of the matter, the decisions referred by the petitioner regarding amendment of pleading has no application in the instant case, but facts remains whether some facts admitted by the petitioners in miscellaneous case in their main application can be deleted after a long time substituting a new facts which already created right in favour of the opposite party. In this case, the petitioner 

 in miscellaneous case at paragraph No. 2 clearly stated that: 

 13. By the proposed amendment, the petitioner in miscellaneous case deleted the date of knowledge as mentioned in Clause-'s' of the proposed amendment and also deleted the statement in same paragraph "বিগত ২০০৩ ইং সনের ডিসেম্বর মাসের শেষ সপ্তাহে". This two dates stated in the main application relating to cause of auction for filing of the miscellaneous case and filing of the Title Suit No. 158 of 2005. By the amendment admittedly, we find that the nature and character of the original application has not been changed, but the petitioners in miscellaneous case once admitted the fact of their knowledge from "Daily Inailab" and also stated name of a month thereafter, so admission made by the petitioners in the original application about date of knowledge cannot be allowed to change the same by subsequent amendment giving a go bye to such admission, bringing a new date of knowledge. In the present case, the deletion of such fact as stated in Clause-'ঙ' and ‘চ’ of the application for amendment of their main application cannot be entertained. 

 17. The execution court is directed to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2009 within 3(three) months excluding the amendment made in Clauses-'ঙ' and 'চ'.
